title: A Ramp to Better Healthcare
body: A 72-year-old woman visiting a district hospital has to climb stairs to reach the Outpatient Department because there is no ramp or handrail. A man in a wheelchair cannot enter the building at all, and a visually impaired visitor cannot find departments because there are no tactile paths or Braille signs. Patients and families raise the issue with hospital authorities and local representatives, and a disability rights organisation highlights it in newspapers and on social media. The district administration asks the Public Works Department and the Health Department to inspect the hospital. After consulting doctors, staff, architects, organisations working with persons with disabilities, senior citizens and residents, a plan is prepared. The government approves funds for ramps, lifts, handrails, tactile pathways, accessible toilets and clear signboards, and the work is completed so that the hospital becomes easier to use for everyone.
